note: H1 — the open question the C2 author raised and could not settle from geometry — is answered by looking at the rendered board. The paragraph is an engineering note, not product copy.

rows.why: H1 ANSWERED BY THE SCREENSHOT. The C2 author revealed three paragraphs by growing their clipping parents, and flagged the open question in writing: are they product copy or C4-class annotation? Geometry cannot tell — both look identical to a containment check, which is exactly why the author refused to guess. The rendered board settles it. The string is \"The thread and the prompt you typed stay on screen behind this state. Losing the user's words is a second failure on top of the first.\" No product tells a user that a failure is 'a second failure on top of the first'; it is third-person reasoning ABOUT the design, addressed to whoever is building it — the same shape as the UX-B-32 paragraphs that F03 hid inside the Pages panel. So the C2 grow was right to reveal what was clipped, and this hides the part that should never have been drawn on a product board. delete is visible=false, so the note is preserved, not destroyed. The recovery control 2846:21651 'Continue by hand in the inspector' STAYS revealed — that is the affordance F06 was about.
